{{short description|Chinese electrical engineer (born 1935)}}
{{family name hatnote|[[Yan (surname)|Yan]]|lang=Chinese}}

'''Yan Luguang''' ({{zh|s=严陆光}}; born 6 July 1935) is a Chinese [[electrical engineer]]. He is a research professor and former Director of the Institute of Electrical Engineering of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] (CAS), and served as President of [[Ningbo University]] from 1999 to 2004. He is an academician of the CAS and [[The World Academy of Sciences]], and a foreign member of the [[National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine]].<ref name="Lu2006">{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=koPT8DV6L58C&pg=PA478|title=Science Progress in China|last=Lu|first=Yongxiang|authorlink=Lu Yongxiang (engineer)|date=2006|publisher=Elsevier|isbn=978-0-08-044970-8|page=478}}</ref> Together with physicist [[Chen Chunxian]], he led the development and construction of China's first [[tokamak]].

== Biography ==
Yan was born on 6 July 1935 in [[Beijing]], with his [[Ancestral home (Chinese)|ancestral home]] in [[Dongyang]], [[Zhejiang]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.casad.cas.cn/aca/377/jskxb-200906-t20090624_1808185.html|title=严陆光|website=Chinese Academy of Sciences|access-date=2019-02-04}}</ref> In 1954, he and his older brother Yan Wuguang (严武光) together went to study in the [[Soviet Union]].<ref name=":1" /> He graduated from the [[Moscow Power Engineering Institute]] in 1959.<ref name=":0" />

After returning to China, Yan joined the newly established Institute of Electrical Engineering of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] (CAS). In the early 1970s, Yan joined physicist [[Chen Chunxian]] to lead the development and construction of China's first [[tokamak]], an electromagnetic device used in [[nuclear fusion]]. Their cooperation achieved success in 1973, with the creation of the tokamak CT-6.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://news.sciencenet.cn/htmlnews/2012/7/266675.shtm|title=严济慈之子严陆光院士：格言点亮人生之光|date=2012-07-09|website=Sciencenet.cn|access-date=2019-02-04}}</ref><ref name=":3" /> Yan also participated in the design of the next tokamak device, the Hefei CT-8.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=http://www.chinavitae.com/biography/Yan_Luguang/bio|title=Biography of Yan Luguang|website=China Vitae|access-date=2019-02-04|archive-date=2019-02-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190204122411/http://www.chinavitae.com/biography/Yan_Luguang/bio|url-status=dead}}</ref>

From 1988 to 1999, Yan served as Director of the Institute of Electrical Engineering. He led research in [[superconductivity]], [[maglev]] trains, [[renewable energy]], and [[electric cars]].<ref name="Lu2006" /><ref name=":0" /> He was elected an academician of the CAS in 1991.<ref name=":0" />

On the recommendation of [[Lu Yongxiang (engineer)|Lu Yongxiang]], the president of the CAS, Yan was appointed President of [[Ningbo University]] in 1999. He served in the position until 2004.<ref name=":1" />

==Family==
Yan is the youngest son of [[Yan Jici]], a founder of modern physics in China, and his wife Zhang Zongying (张宗英).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.tuanjiebao.com/tjej/2016-04/05/content_56289.htm|title=严济慈之子严陆光院士回忆 父亲的"严"与"慈"|author=Wang Xinxia 王信霞|date=2016-04-05|work=Tuanjie Bao|access-date=2019-02-02|archive-date=2019-02-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190202061330/http://www.tuanjiebao.com/tjej/2016-04/05/content_56289.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> He has four older brothers, not counting three other siblings who died in infancy. The five Yan brothers all became academics, including Yan Youguang (严又光), the main designer of China's first digital computer, Yan Shuangguang (严双光), an aircraft designer, and Yan Wuguang, a professor at the CAS [[Institute of High Energy Physics]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.todayonhistory.com/people/201804/31391.html|title=严济慈的儿女：个个出身高校 投身科研、教育事业|date=2018-04-10 |website=Todayonhistory.com|access-date=2019-02-02}}</ref> The Yan family has been called the "little academy of science".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://arch.ustc.edu.cn/story/yjc.htm|title=严济慈|website=University of Science and Technology of China|access-date=2019-02-02|archive-date=2005-05-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050505041805/http://arch.ustc.edu.cn/story/yjc.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Yan is married to Lü Xi'en (吕锡恩), a graduate of the [[University of Leningrad]] and an associate professor at the CAS Institute of Chemistry.<ref name=":2" />
